name: Foxborough
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Foxborough, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Foxborough, MA: Light Uptown on the Common, free Santa photos at Patriot Place, the MRPAC Nutcracker and a Grinch skate.
lede: Foxborough lights up its Common the Saturday after Thanksgiving, then fills December with Santa at Patriot Place, holiday shows at the Marilyn Rodman Performing Arts Center and skating by the stadium.
celebrates: Foxborough's season starts with Light Uptown on the Saturday after Thanksgiving, when the town lights the Common and the Foxboro Jaycees help bring Santa and Mrs. Claus to visit the kids. The Jaycees have decorated the Common for more than thirty years with bows, wreaths, garland and lights on the hedges, the bandstand and the lamp posts. A Nativity scene first made in the 1950s goes up on the bandstand, and each December the Jaycees lead caroling there with the Foxboro High School Christmas Chorus Band. At Patriot Place, families find Santa's Wonderland at Bass Pro Shops and an outdoor skating rink.
lastyear: In 2025 the Foxboro Jaycees again helped Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive at Light Uptown on the Common, and they expanded the Nativity on the bandstand with a matching vintage set from the La Salette Shrine in Enfield, New Hampshire. The Foxborough Community Center held a free Holiday Craft Fair on November 29 as part of Light Uptown, and the Foxborough Recreation Department ran a family bus trip to Cirque Dreams Holidaze at PPAC on December 21.
facts: Foxborough was settled in 1704 and incorporated on June 10, 1778, in the middle of the Revolutionary War. It is named for Charles James Fox, a British Whig who spoke up for the American colonies. The bandstand on Foxboro Common, where the Nativity stands each December, was built by the Jaycees in 1972, and the Jaycees have cared for the Nativity set since the late 1980s, with a full refurbishment in 2020.
trains: Foxborough has its own MBTA Commuter Rail stop, Foxboro station by Gillette Stadium, on the Franklin/Foxboro Line. Gillette Stadium lists 10 weekday round trips between Foxboro and South Station in Boston, and the MBTA notes that the Foxboro stop is served on weekdays only. That makes a weekday train trip into Boston possible straight from Patriot Place, without driving into the city. Edaville in Carver runs a Christmas train through its festival of lights, with general admission that includes a ride on the Holiday Express.

faq: When is the Foxborough tree lighting?

Foxborough lights its Common at Light Uptown, held on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. The Foxboro Jaycees decorate the Common that morning and help bring Santa and Mrs. Claus to visit the kids in the afternoon and evening. The Community Center has paired the day with a free holiday craft fair in past years.
Where can kids see Santa in Foxborough?

Santa comes to Light Uptown on the Common the Saturday after Thanksgiving. Through Christmas Eve, Bass Pro Shops at Patriot Place runs Santa's Wonderland, with a free 4x6 photo and a free video for every family and free reservations a week ahead. The Hockomock Area YMCA also hosts a Fun With Santa night.
Is there caroling on Foxboro Common?

Yes. For more than thirty years the Foxboro Jaycees have invited the town to sing Christmas carols at the bandstand on Foxboro Common at 6 pm, with music from the Foxboro High School Christmas Chorus Band, plus hot chocolate and song books. In bad weather it moves into Boyden Library across the street.
Can you take the train to Foxborough?

Yes, on weekdays. Foxboro station by Gillette Stadium is on the MBTA Franklin/Foxboro Line, and Gillette Stadium lists 10 weekday round trips to South Station. The MBTA says trains stop at Foxboro on weekdays only, so weekend visitors to Light Uptown or Patriot Place will need to drive.
